detailed_feedback.in_text_citation_format: The in-text citations are inconsistent, with some using bracketed numbers, others embedded author-year formats, and some lacking parentheses or proper punctuation. Adopting a uniform style such as author-year (e.g., (Author, Year)) throughout the manuscript will improve clarity and professionalism.
detailed_feedback.reference_list_format: The reference list contains entries with inconsistent formatting: some include DOIs, others omit them; journal names are sometimes italicized, sometimes not; volume, issue, and page numbers are inconsistently presented. Standardizing all references according to a recognized style guide (e.g., APA 7th edition) will enhance readability and scholarly rigor.
detailed_feedback.citation_style_consistency: The manuscript exhibits mixed citation styles, blending numeric and author-year formats. Consistent application of a single style (preferably author-year for academic papers) across all sections will improve coherence.
detailed_feedback.reference_completeness: Many references lack complete bibliographic details such as volume, issue, pages, or publication years. Ensuring all references are complete will facilitate source verification and uphold academic standards.
detailed_feedback.doi_url_formatting: DOIs are inconsistently formatted; some include the 'https://doi.org/' prefix, others do not. Uniform formatting with the prefix improves accessibility and aligns with best practices.
detailed_feedback.author_name_formatting: Author names are inconsistently formatted—some with full names, others with initials. Standardizing to surname followed by initials (e.g., Smith J.) ensures clarity and uniformity.
detailed_feedback.publication_date_formatting: Publication dates vary in presentation, with some including month and year, others only year. Consistent date formatting (e.g., Year) enhances chronological clarity.
detailed_feedback.journal_name_formatting: Journal names are inconsistently italicized and abbreviated. Applying a uniform style (e.g., italics for journal titles, full names) improves visual consistency.
detailed_feedback.volume_issue_page_formatting: Volume, issue, and page numbers are inconsistently formatted; some missing parentheses or page ranges. Standard formatting (e.g., Vol(issue), pages) improves source identification.
detailed_feedback.cross_reference_accuracy: In-text citations sometimes do not match reference list entries in numbering or author-year details. Cross-checking all citations ensures accuracy and prevents confusion.

summary: Overall, the manuscript demonstrates a need for significant improvement in citation formatting and consistency. Adopting a standardized referencing style, ensuring complete bibliographic details, and harmonizing in-text citation formats will greatly enhance the scholarly quality and professionalism of the document. Implementing these changes will facilitate source verification, improve readability, and align with academic standards.
